mechanism_claims.claim_text: B22/B22a rapidly bind bacteria, permeabilize the cytoplasmic membrane, and cause membrane blebbing/cell-shape collapse at micromolar concentrations.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Representative imaging supports mechanism; exact image-derived intensity traces are preserved by locator rather than re-digitized.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: B22/B22a induce oxidative stress/ROS that contributes to growth inhibition and killing; ROS scavengers/iron chelation and SodA overexpression reduce killing.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=7:FIG 7; xml:fig=8:FIG 8; xml:sec=11:B22a triggers oxidative stress in V. cholerae; xml:sec=12:ROS scavengers and superoxide dismutase suppress B22-mediated cell death

mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism is strongest for observed ROS-associated killing/growth suppression; not normalized into a universal AMP mechanism outside the tested cathelicidin variants.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Higher-order oligomerization is not required for growth inhibition because B22m1, a phenylalanine-to-alanine variant with smaller structures, still reduced growth and induced ROS.
